cards.explanation: The answer is that David asks the LORD not to rebuke him in anger. He opens with “O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.” No greeting and no warm-up, he goes straight to the point. I think when you're hurting that much, small talk can wait, friends.

The answer is sin. David says, “there is no rest in my bones because of my sin.” He doesn't point at anybody else here. He owns it, and that takes some courage, friends. He'll say it again in verse 18, so keep your ears open.

The answer is mourning all day long. David says, “I am bent and brought low; all day long I go about mourning.” It's not a bad hour or two. It's all day long. I think that's a heavy way to live, friends.

The answer is True! David says, “O Lord, my every desire is before You; my groaning is not hidden from You.” In the middle of all that pain, he knows he's heard. Nothing he groans is lost. That's worth holding onto, friends.

The answer is the light of his eyes. David says, “My heart pounds, my strength fails, and even the light of my eyes has faded.” Notice that little word “even.” The list keeps going. I think he's running on empty.

The answer is False. David says, “My beloved and friends shun my disease, and my kinsmen stand at a distance.” The people closest to him keep their distance. I think that would sting on top of the pain, friends.

The answer is that he does not open his mouth. David says, “…like a mute man, I do not open my mouth.” He adds that he's like a man whose mouth offers no reply. While they plot, he stays quiet. Me, I can't stay quiet when a timer goes off.

The answer is True. David says, “I wait for You, O LORD; You will answer, O Lord my God.” He's quiet toward his enemies, but he isn't quiet toward the LORD. He waits, and he says the LORD will answer. That's hope in the middle of the hurt, friends.
The answer is iniquity. David says, “Yes, I confess my iniquity; I am troubled by my sin.” He doesn't dodge or dress it up. That's a hard thing to do, friends.
The answer is False. David says, “Yes, I confess my iniquity; I am troubled by my sin.” He's not shrugging it off. I think it's an honest, heavy moment, friends.

The answer is that they hate him without reason. David says, “Many are my enemies without cause, and many hate me without reason.” He's not saying they have a good reason and he's ignoring it. He says they have none. Verse 20 tells us more about what they do.

The answer is that David asks the LORD not to forsake him or be far. He prays, “Do not forsake me, O LORD; be not far from me, O my God.” After all that groaning, he asks the LORD to stay close. I think that tells us a lot, friends.

The answer is Savior. The last line is “Come quickly to help me, O Lord my Savior.” He ends the whole psalm with that one word for the Lord. After all the pain, that's where he lands, friends. I'd call that a strong finish.
